> Indeed, I think it's possible to reduce the frequency of `_clear_cache`, but as I mentioned in [#115550 (comment)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115550#issuecomment-3825635801), I think it would be better to make TrackCache retention an optional property, such as `keep_cache`.
> 
> Keeping cache after stopping causes memory to be occupied even when the player is stopped.

Yes, and I'd argue that's exactly the point of the cache. Also If the node is just stopped and not destroyed it's probably going to be reused.

> But, the main problem for keeping cache is that TrackCache continues to hold references. For example, if you delete a scene object after stopping the AnimationPlayer, the remaining reference in the cache could unintentionally create an orphan object.
> 
> While both issues can be addressed by explicitly calling `clear_cache()`, the former is simply a performance issue, whereas the latter has the potential to cause errors.
> 
> Conversely, if there were an implementation that avoided cases where orphan objects are created (such as having the AnimationMixer detect changes to the scene or resources), there would be no need for it to be an optional property.
> 
> In any case, we must carefully consider any changes to the behavior of _clear_cache. Besides that, as I mentioned in [#115550 (comment)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115550#issuecomment-3825635801), I think it would be better to have a separate method for creating a cache even while the player is stopped.

I see your point.
It seems to me that this would be a problem only with TrackCacheAudio's audio_stream_playback unless I'm missing something. audio_stream seems owned by the cache itself and gets destroyed when the AnimationPlayer is destroyed.
So I've added a cleanup in _clear_audio_streams().
It does mean iterating the tracks and cleaning them selectively but I couldn't measure any performance difference in my tests, with hundreds of entities.
Not sure whether this is the best approach as I don't know the full animator architecture, so I leave it to your judgement.

Disclosure: this last edit was done with AI, but it's just a few lines anyway.

For now, I think it's ready for review regarding `_clear_cache()`. Since feature freeze for 4.7 has already passed, we'll review it during the animation meeting for 4.8. @Ryan-000 Can you review it if you have time as a contributor for the similar area?

Also, it would be helpful to include the following two things:
- Implementation of the `make_cache()` function for cases where you want to create a cache before calling `play()`
- Documentation explaining that the cache is not deleted by `stop()`, so you need to explicitly call `clear_cache()`

Thanks for the reviews @TokageItLab
However, I'd like to push back on the 4.8 deferral.
This PR doesn't introduce any new behavior, it just removes an unintended performance penalty that was happening silently.
The animation tracks cache was being cleared on every stop and empty queue, which was never documented as a guarantee or even a deliberate design choice. From the user's perspective nothing changes.
I can surely add this behaviour on the docs but it seems superfluous to me as the cache-clearing behavior was never documented.

On the contrary a `make_cache()` function would be a new feature as it would introduce a new API, and it would be a reasonable discussion for 4.8. I also think this would be beyond the scope of this PR, which aims just to fix a performance problem.
The two could be addressed independently: this PR for 4.7, and a make_cache() API discussion for 4.8.
It seems counterproductive to me to block a performance fix in favor of a new API that doesn't exist yet.

Also I was really hoping for this to be included in 4.7, hence my quick responses and iterations of the PR. I'd really prefer to stay on official builds rather than maintaining my own fork.

Could this be reconsidered for 4.7? It seems well within the scope of what a performance fix should be, and deferring it means users hit this performance wall for another full release cycle.

> Conversely, if there were an implementation that avoided cases where orphan objects are created (such as having the AnimationMixer detect changes to the scene or resources), there would be no need for it to be an optional property.

I agree. I think the issue is that `AnimationMixer::_update_caches` does not track the node's path, so it cannot invalidate a `TrackCache` when the node's ancestry changes.

For example if an animated node is removed from the scene tree, like with `node->get_parent()->remove_child(node)`, it will still be animated even though it is no longer part of the scene.

Another example is an animated node is reparented, the animation will continue to work because `TrackCache::object_id` is still valid. 
However, if that same tree is packed into a `PackedScene` and instantiated again, `AnimationMixer` will fail to resolve the `NodePath` and report an error, which is inconsistent.

> Keeping cache after stopping causes memory to be occupied even when the player is stopped.

IMO, it is worth keeping the cache after stopping, since rebuilding it can become expensive very quickly, especially with skeletal animations.

While I agree with you that the hierarchy tracking issue is a problem, it is a pre-existing problem that was also present before this PR. My changes neither introduce it nor make it worse.

As for the breaks compat label/possibility of bugs: the previous cache clearing behavior was never documented as a guarantee, just an implementation detail that some workflows may have inadvertently relied on. That's the kind of compat break that comes with any bug fix, and I think it's the right tradeoff here.

The edge cases @Ryan-000 describes are worth addressing, but they can be tracked separately. They are not regressions introduced by this PR and are beyond its scope.

With that said, I think we may be framing this incorrectly. The distinction between "enhancement" and "bug fix" matters here.
This PR doesn't implement a faster algorithm: it stops the engine from eagerly discarding valid cached data it had no reason to discard, which defeats the purpose of a cache in the first place.
Overly eager cache invalidation that causes measurable performance degradation is a bug in the same way a memory leak is: you could frame fixing either one as a "performance enhancement", but the root cause is incorrect behavior, not missing optimization.

@reduz I'd value your perspective on the bug vs enhancement framing here, and whether this meets the bar for 4.7
Hi, @h1v9, this issue is listed as breaks compat. Can you edit the main issue text to point to the proposal (and bug issue) that this PR is fixing?

> Hi, @h1v9, this issue is listed as breaks compat. Can you edit the main issue text to point to the proposal (and bug issue) that this PR is fixing?

Hey @lyuma 
I think the break compat label is out of place here, I'll quote what I wrote in my previous message:
> As for the breaks compat label/possibility of bugs: the previous cache clearing behavior was never documented as a guarantee, just an implementation detail that some workflows may have inadvertently relied on. That's the kind of compat break that comes with any bug fix, and I think it's the right tradeoff here.

There's no issue relative to this PR as this is a problem I incurred into myself, so I just decided to go ahead and fix it.
To sum it up the problem is that the AnimationMixer clears the cache any time the playback is stopped, causing it to be rebuilt every time the animations resume. This was absolutely destroying performance in my project, especially on mobile.

If there are projects that leave AnimationPlayer in the scene even after they have stopped (in spite of never be played again), this PR will cause a performance degradation by memory usage and it is break compatibility; In other words, if making current this PR state the default behavior and you want to inform users to explicitly call `clear_cache()`, it should be break compatibility. Therefore, we have decided that this feature should be optional.

Specifically, the AnimationPlayer will likely need to include a property such as `clear_cache_on_stop`. Then, to maintain compatibility, the default value should be `true`. Once that’s done, we should be able to remove the “breaks compat” label and assess whether the changes can be merged.

> If there are projects that leave AnimationPlayer in the scene even after they have stopped (in spite of never be played again), this PR will cause a performance degradation by memory usage and it is break compatibility; In other words, if making current this PR state the default behavior and you want to inform users to explicitly call `clear_cache()`, it should be break compatibility. Therefore, we have decided that this feature should be optional.
> 
> Specifically, the AnimationPlayer will likely need to include a property such as `clear_cache_on_stop`. Then, to maintain compatibility, the default value should be `true`. Once that’s done, we should be able to remove the “breaks compat” label and assess whether the changes can be merged.

I'm happy to implement `clear_cache_on_stop`, but before I do I'd like to understand the compatibility reasoning a bit better.

1. Is the memory footprint of a stopped AnimationPlayer documented anywhere? If not, on what basis can users depend on it and how is that different from any other internal optimization that would also change memory usage?

2. A cache by definition exists to avoid redundant work. Isn't the natural assumption that a cache persists until explicitly cleared, rather than being silently discarded on stop? If the clearing behavior was never documented, why is that the assumed default rather than the other way around?

Let me know how you'd like to proceed and I'll implement accordingly.

If I had to say, it is this part of the AnimationMixer documentation:

```xml
<method name="clear_caches">
	<return type="void" />
	<description>
		[AnimationMixer] caches animated nodes. It may not notice if a node disappears; [method clear_caches] forces it to update the cache again.
	</description>
</method>
```

but it does not mention memory usage. If we make improvement to monitor the scene structure, this documentation would eventually become outdated.

Currently, it does not strain memory usage upon stopping, so the user does not need to worry about it. Rather, the implementation you are attempting to make is what might cause users to become aware for the first time that cache remains and strains memory when stopped. Therefore, you should be the one to write about memory and cache generation during playback in the description of the `clear_cache_on_stop()` method.

> Isn't the natural assumption that a cache persists until explicitly cleared, rather than being silently discarded on stop?

That may be the case for you and some users, but since this is behavior that has existed for a long time, we need to maintain compatibility. There is no guarantee that past projects, where the cache was automatically deleted, will not be broken by the cache not being deleted.

If this PR fixes clearly broken behavior, it can be considered a simple fix rather than a breaking change, but this PR is not so. As I mentioned above with the example of the AnimationPlayer that never restarts, there are cases where clearing the cache makes more sense and there may be existing projects that depend on it.

Godot is not used only by you, so we must avoid implementations that could break existing projects as much as possible.

@TokageItLab Thank you for the approval. I want to be honest though: this process has been frustrating.

I flagged a real performance problem, iterated quickly, addressed every technical objection that was raised, and implemented what was asked. PR #118867 was merged into 4.7 on April 23, six days after the feature freeze, carrying both the enhancement and performance labels, and changes the default behavior of navmesh baking outright for every user, no toggle, no opt-in, no way to revert.
So the freeze policy clearly isn't being applied uniformly.

My PR, with clear_cache_on_stop defaulting to true, changes nothing for anyone who doesn't flip the switch. It is by every measurable standard the less invasive change. I'd genuinely like to understand the distinction.

I'd rather contribute to official builds than maintain my own fork. But it honestly makes you wonder why even bother when every hoop just leads to another.

As a supplement, #118867 was merged before beta1. This PR was submitted after beta1. Also #105329 was reviewed before the feature freeze, and #118867 was resubmitted to follow with merging #105329 by the maintainer.

Furthermore, since #118867 is a completely internal fix (means there is no reason to intentionally turn off #118867), it is very unlikely to break existing projects.

In contrast, the initial state of this PR had the potential to break existing projects. Because the past behavior was intentional, adding an option is necessary to prevent breaking existing projects. Adding an option is definitely a feature addition, not internal fix.

@TokageItLab Noted.
For the record: the feature freeze was announced April 17. https://godotengine.org/article/dev-snapshot-godot-4-7-dev-5/
#118867 was merged April 23, six days into the freeze. It being approved 1 year before doesn't mean much to me, as I assume the codebase changed a lot during 1 year.
This PR was submitted April 24. Same day as the beta release. https://godotengine.org/article/dev-snapshot-godot-4-7-beta-1/
And it's a new feature because you requested it as such.

I didn't mention this before, as I just wanted to get this approved, but it might be worth doing it now: I genuinely think we're choosing the wrong approach here.
While it is true that not clearing the cache increases memory usage when stopped, we're talking at worst tens of kilobytes, a negligible amount. Someone relying on this means they went out of their way to measure AnimationPlayer memory usage when running and when stopped, as this is not even documented anywhere.
I challenge you to find anyone actually relying on this lower memory usage when stopped.
And of course I know the situation worsens with many entities, but that's exactly when deleting the cache destroys performance.

On the other side I'm sure there's plenty of projects leaving performance on the table because of cache clearing without even knowing it.
And finding it out is non-trivial: it requires recompiling the engine with debug symbols and attaching a profiler.
Even with the current property, since it's set as default to true, most users won't be able to leverage the peformance improvement as they won't even know it's needed.

To me the right approach is obvious: keep the cache as default and just document that stop doesn't clear it automatically anymore. The clear_caches() method is there anyways if anyone was relying on this.
A cache that gets cleared on every stop is not a cache. It's a temporary allocation that gets discarded the moment it could start paying for itself.

Don't get me wrong, I'm done pushing for 4.7 as it's clear that a decision has already been made. I'll just keep maintaining my own build.
Anyone who doesn't know to disable clear_cache_on_stop will keep hitting this wall. Either way, users pay the cost.
Thanks! Sorry to keep you waiting!
